english.title: Owner / master discharge oil / mixture containing oil into United Kingdom national waters
english.standardoffencewording:

(A)_[owner]_
(B)_[master]_

of a ship, namely **(..SPECIFY SHIP..), from which there was a relevant discharge,

(C)_[the ship being an offshore installation and the discharge being into United Kingdom national waters which were navigable by sea-going ships]_

english.legislation: Contrary to section 131(1)(a) and (3) of the Merchant Shipping Act 1995.

english.notes:
(i) See section 131(A1) of the Merchant Shipping Act 1995, for definition of "relevant discharge" and other wordings are further defined in section 131.
(ii) Where there is a relevant discharge, subject to the provisions of Chapter II after section 131 of the Merchant Shipping Act 1995, the following shall be guilty of an offence, (a) the owner or master of the ship, unless he proves that the discharge took place and was caused as mentioned in paragraph (b); (b) if the discharge from the ship takes place in the course of a transfer of oil to or from another ship or a place on land and is caused by the act or omission of any person in charge of any apparatus in that other ship or that place, the owner or master of that other ship or, as the case may be, the occupier of that place.
(iii) Subsection 1 does not apply to any discharge from an offshore installation which is made into the sea and is of a kind or is made in circumstances for the time being prescribed in regulations made by the Secretary of State - section 131(2)
(iv) see subsections (3A)(4)(5)(6) for definitions
(v) See section 132 for further defences

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding £250,000.
Indictment: A fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
